If a driver writes in complaining about a missing bonus, you can find all the bonuses the driver is enrolled in from [Admin V1|https://admin.bolt.eu/admin/] > Campaigns> Fleet campaigns > [enrolment into periods|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet_campaign/PeriodEnrollment/]. If you have a dispute on if a driver completed a bonus or not, please reach out to [Tech Support.|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/2] 
Note that the Commerce Billing team does not determine if a driver wins a bonus or not, we only ensure that won bonuses are added to drivers accounts. If there is an issue with the bonus completion, we cannot assist you.

*Brief overview:* In Romania ride hailing providers have to have a “Technical Approval” by an authority (ADR). Operators of the digital platform have to notify ADR of any development, modification of operating data and operational procedures. Bolt informed the ADR about the new feature ““verifying the identity of the driver” and the regulator wants a report to analyse the impact of this change and also if the security and operation requirements of the digital platform are still met. PP team got in touch with an IT auditor and the auditor requests a “*Privacy opinion*”

I asks PP team to check/specify what information the auditor requested and [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] will reach out to the auditor.  PP and the audit team will also interview *Daniel Berbece (*Senior Backend Engineer @ Verification Team).

_Annex No. 1 Anti-corruption clause of the Veolia group_



_1.1 When performing this Agreement, the contracting parties undertake to strictly comply with all applicable and valid legal regulations regarding business ethics, including regulations prohibiting bribery of public officials and private individuals, illegal influence and money laundering, and in particular:_



_a)  French anti-corruption law No. 2016-1691 ("Sapin II law") on transparency, the fight against corruption and the modernization of economic life of 9 December 2016._



_b) Act of the Czech Republic No. 418/2011 Coll., on criminal liability of legal entities and proceedings against them, as amended._



_1.2 The contracting parties undertake to implement and implement all necessary and reasonable measures to prevent corruption._

_1.4 If the Customer has reasonable grounds to believe that Bolt has violated any provision of this clause, it is entitled to suspend the performance of this Agreement by simple notice without prior notice for as long as the Customer considers necessary to investigate the conduct in question, without incurring any liability of the Customer for such suspension or any obligation of the Customer to Bolt. _1.5 If Bolt proves to be in breach of any obligation set forth in this clause above, Customer may immediately terminate this Agreement by withdrawal or termination with immediate effect and without incurring any liability to Bolt._

Hi [~accountid:5d95f00136d2520dde7ede17]!

We finally found a solution to the bailiff requests in LT.

* Bolt has an obligation to comply with bailiffs’ requests. 
* But in practice, they seem to be ineffective and hardly implementable (because of the special nature of Bolt's relations with drivers, dynamic income, payments before taxes, lack of information on how much is deducted from gross payments, info about other income courses etc.). Therefore, there is a very low risk of any kind of sanctions (this is the reason why Bolt has not gotten any fines for the last 9 years). 
* But to minimize legal risks, we shall not ignore such requests, instead, we provide a  standard response, please see the template here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U6EJA_Xf0Gdccrpxtunt9C9w4LG710_6/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1U6EJA_Xf0Gdccrpxtunt9C9w4LG710_6/edit|smart-link]  

In the reply, we provide all the arguments why we cannot make deductions and disclose the driver account details where payments are made so that a bailiff could make any deductions from those funds himself/herself. If you are interested, you can read the opinion prepared by external counsels (below). 

[^Compliance with bailiff orders in LT.pdf]

*Product spec:*

We should add a small widget to admin-panel (would be displayed only on non-created bulk-group - clone/new).
This widget would have following fields:

* {{Distribution (Share of population)}}
* {{Discounts}} - will accept a list of percentage numbers
* {{Set 100% holdouts}}  - checkbox
* {{Is opt in}}  - checkbox
* {{Button}}

On button click:
For each test _(for budget bins there are one test for each cohort)_ we will add new RH targeted campaigns with each of the discounts values - so, if {{Discounts}}  field had values {{10%}} and {{20%}} we will add 2 DEX campaigns to each test with corresponding discount. The fields for each DEX campaign would be set:

* {{Spend objective = DEX}}
* {{Holdout percantage}} for treatment, if checkbox is checked
* {{Is opt-in}} if checkbox is checked
* {{Distribution}} in a treatment
* {{Discount}}
* {{Treatment label}}  as {{DEX}} in a treatment


*Hidden logic holdouts alert:*
If holdout is set to yes - we also need to assign to holdout some % of the control group (so that we have some benchmark for comparison).this some % = rounded *up(* distribution of DEX treatment if it is assigned to holdout/ distribution of a control group treatment), I used ceil for rounding
[Example 1|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/campaign-targeting/tests/rides_and_rental/1191964]:
Here {{distribution of DEX treatment if it is assigned to holdout}}  = 2
{{distribution of a control group treatment}}  = 25
{{ % of the control group to be assigned to holdout}}  = 2/25 = 0.08 or 8% => control group holdout is 8
[Example 2|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/campaign-targeting/tests/rides_and_rental/1191968]:
Here {{distribution of DEX treatment if it is assigned to holdout}}  = 2
{{distribution of a control group treatment}}  = 20
{{ % of the control group to be assigned to holdout}}  = 2/20 = 0.1 or 10% => control group % for holdout is 8Idea is that we have in holdout same % of the total population from control group as per each Discount Exploration treatment that is assigned to holdout

{noformat}#!/bin/bash
set -e

CONTEXT=$1
#DRY_RUN="--dry-run=client"
SLEEP="15"
BATCH_SIZE="15"
IDX=0

if [[ -z "${CONTEXT}" ]]; then
  echo "Missing input parameters, at least 1 required: context"
  exit 1;
fi

NEWEST_VERSION=$(kubectl --context ${CONTEXT} get nodes -l karpenter.sh/registered=true -o custom-columns="VERSION:.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion" --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 1)

echo "Newest version is ${NEWEST_VERSION}"
echo ""

NODES_TO_RECYCLE=$(kubectl --context ${CONTEXT} get nodes -l karpenter.sh/registered=true -o jsonpath="{range .items[?(@.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion != '${NEWEST_VERSION}')]}{.metadata.name}{'\n'}{end}")

if [[ -z $NODES_TO_RECYCLE ]]; then
  echo "No nodes to recycle"
  exit 0;
else
  echo "Nodes to be recycled:"
  echo "${NODES_TO_RECYCLE}"
fi

date

for NODE in $NODES_TO_RECYCLE; do
    ((IDX=IDX+1))
    if [[ "${IDX}" -gt "${BATCH_SIZE}" ]]
    then
        echo "Batch of ${BATCH_SIZE} is finished"
        sleep 120
    fi

    echo ""
    echo "[${IDX}]: Draining node $NODE with '$DRY_RUN' option"
    
    if [[ "${IDX}" -gt "0" ]]
    then
      echo "Waiting for ${SLEEP}s..."
      sleep ${SLEEP}
    fi

    kubectl --context ${CONTEXT} drain ${DRY_RUN} $NODE --delete-emptydir-data --ignore-daemonsets
done

*Assessment of liability in relation to cleaning fees*

Our Passenger T&Cs (section 4.7) state the following which sets out the liability of the passenger for any damages that the passenger has caused to the vehicle: _If you have requested transport services using the Bolt app and cause damage to the driver’s vehicle or its furnishing (among else, by blemishing or staining the vehicle or causing the vehicle to stink), the driver will have the right to require you to pay a penalty of 50 EUR and require compensation for any damages exceeding the penalty. If you do not pay the penalty and/or compensate the damage, Bolt may pursue the claims on behalf of the provider of the transport service._ 

Based on this, the driver has a right to request payment and the rider is liable to compensate the driver for any damages above 50 EUR (or 500 SEK for Sweden). 

Our Driver T&Cs (section 4.14) state the similar from a Driver perspective and further clarifies that Bolt holds no liability in case of damages to the Driver vehicle: _If, in the course of the provision of the Transportation Services, a Passenger or its co-passengers negligently damage the vehicle or its furnishing (among else, by blemishing or staining the vehicle or causing the vehicle to stink), you shall have the right to request the Passenger to pay a penalty up to 50 EUR and request compensation for any damages exceeding the penalty. If the Passenger does not consent to paying the penalty and/or compensating the damage, you must notify us and we will then try to collect penalty and/or relevant costs on the your behalf from the Passenger._ +_However, bear in mind that we are not taking any liability for direct or indirect damages in relation to cleaning or maintenance of the vehicle caused by Passenger._+

*Conclusion: Driver can request payment from Rider for any direct damages caused by the Rider. Bolt holds no liability in relation to such costs but may help the Driver in receiving payment from the Rider.*

*Questions to client*:

* Can you give me an idea of the volume of discounts Bolt intends to revoke? (e.g. estimated number of affected business accounts, EUR impact, timeline etc)

*Responses*: 


*Expand*

*Guilherme Franciulli* 
* Can you give me an idea of the volume of discounts Bolt intends to revoke? (e.g. estimated number of affected business accounts, EUR impact, timeline etc)
unclear. it wasn't an initiative driven by us. we deployed in our system, but it was requested by Business product itself to have this integration with Fraud where we would remove discounts from users that were abusing. the initial focus was to target users that sign up to multiple business companies to continue benefiting from 25,50,75% discounts in the first orders that were given to each business company account. I can query some high level numbers, but it will be very rough estimates. would you be interested in that?
* Are the discounts in question only related to ride-hailing, or are there specific examples in other verticals?
Rides only. but not sure if that will always be the case. might need to ask Business Product people if they're planning to expand to Food or other verticals.
* Are we talking about general discounts, or bolt business 'coupons'?
Business people might be the best to match the exact wording. the way that I know how to describe is that it's the discounts that are given to new company accounts when they sign up. we don't remove the discounts from the company. we just remove the discounts from the user at the order request level. if the company has legit users, company still gets to use the discount in the end.
* Can you share why the preference would be to disable a discount and not suspend the fraudulent user/business account?
when handling discount abuse there's no need to reject the user as a whole since we can still get GMV from such users. purpose here is just to avoid giving discounts to them. these order searches where we remove the discount, some of them still happen where the user simply pays the full price.
*Guilherme Franciulli*  
here's how an abuser looks like:
[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/users/193545080?tab=instruments|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/commerce-payment/users/193545080?tab=instruments]user has 15 different business companies in their payment method. 12 of them used the same signup code (LATO60) to get discounts.
*Guilherme Franciulli*  
* Can you give me an idea of the volume of discounts Bolt intends to revoke? (e.g. estimated number of affected business accounts, EUR impact, timeline etc)
getting back to this, actually it will be pretty tough to get an estimate here. because we're not revoking the discounts from the companies. code it only ends up being unused if the whole company is fraudulent. meaning that all of the company users have other related companies that used discounts before. so there's no proper way for me to find you a number here since I won't know how many of these companies will be fully stopped from using discounts. perhaps Business people can have estimates as they were the ones that pushed this development. they might know better the size of the problem. Fraud acted as a supporter.
*Guilherme Franciulli*  
I've queried the number of triggers per week we had since launching this checkpoint. also the number of distinct users and the number of distinct companies.important to highlight that this checkpoint runs at the order search. an order search doesn't necessarily converts to an order. an user trying to force their way might do multiple order searches.I think this should help giving an idea of impact. less than 100 companies per week is the number we had in the past two weeks since launching. these companies are likely all fraudulent, meaning that they'll probably be fully blocked from using discount for not having any legit user.Screenshot 2023-10-24 at 16.11.40.png

Hey [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048], thanks for pointing this out.

I would say that it would be disproportionate initially, but I agree that we first have to check what existed before. What I mean is this: biometrics is one of the most intrusive means of carrying out this type of control and could initially be replaced by another (such as magnetic access cards). So, if there is no control at all (or if there is some manual control, with people signing in at the entrance, for example), I would say that it is intrusive. On the other hand, if there is already entry control via magnetic card and there have still been errors, then it's best to request a copy of the internal audit to understand why the previous system didn't work. My suggestion is that we start the PPRA. (and possibly DPIA, etc.) only after understanding the results of this audit, not least so that we can eventually make suggestions without doing unnecessary work.

* The counterparty is a company operating a platform for talents and entrepreneurs (i.e. some end users engaged in some work related activities) on which it offers benefits, services, subscriptions and some tools provided by its partners to its customers. So they act as an intermediary connecting users of their platform and partners.
* The company will provide their customers with the access to ride-hailing services by using Bolt Business. 
* The company will offer packages containing a credit that will allow users to do as many rides as possible within the provided limit.
* How it would work in practice: 
** user buys a package on the company’s platform, 
** the company supplies Bolt with the list of users who bought packages and the limits that should apply to them, 
** Bolt adds the limit to these users as if they were employees of this company using Bolt Business,
** the company pays Bolt at the end of the month for the rides taken by users + commission (if criteria is met),
** if the user exceeds the limit provided by the company the user will need to pay for the rides after the limit is exhausted from their private funds.

The formula for calculation is:

Commission calculation: commission is calculated from this:



Final price (6717.10€) + Cancellation fee (34.20€) = 6751.30€.



25% from that is 1687.83€.



Due to the rounding error (we calculate 25% from each ride and then sum it up vs. taking 25% from the total) he actually gained an extra 0.27€ thanks to the summed-up commission amount being slightly smaller.

How long such AB-test usually last and in which countries are they planned in?In general, Omnibus makes an exception to the 30-days-lowest price in case it's a *real personalised price reduction*. No certain definition for real personalised price reduction is given in the Omnibus directive, however, the European Commission explains that a typical example of _such price reductions are those resulting from the consumer’s prior purchases with the seller concerned_. Please note that in case the personalised price reduction is accessible to *many or the majority* of customers, it *will not go under the real personalised price reduction.* Also, it is recommended that we inform users (I don't we think we plan to do this?) when the price reduction displayed to them is personalised on the basis of the user’s prior purchases (and behaviour).

# Instead, try to choose the polygon/region of the destination address, so the courier just understands the region/area to which the delivery was made. Screenshots from maps with the address should not be shared.
# In case the courier needs a specific location to defend a penalty or claim, the sharing of the exact address should be approved by the legal team.

Instead, I would recommend encouraging the drivers to download their tax documents as promptly as possible, placing the responsibility on them to initiate a new contact with us. We can mark the ticket as 'pending,' granting drivers a generous 3-day window to respond to the same ticket and provide updates. This way, we empower drivers to take charge of these actions, sparing our CS from the need to revisit the ticket and make follow-ups to check if the documents have already been downloaded.

{noformat}with summary as (
select 
etl.driver_country as country,
etl.id, 
etl.from_vat_code,
etl.sum,
etl.sum_with_vat,
etl.vat_sum,
fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code as driver_vat_code,
fd.invoice_issuer_is_liable_to_vat as driver_vat_liability,
fc.vat_code as company_vat_code,
fc.is_liable_to_vat as company_vat_liability,
ifc.invoicing_strategy 
from ng_public.etl_billing_invoicing_rides_user etl
left join ng_public.fleet_driver fd on fd.id = etl.driver_id and etl.from_type = 'ride_hailing_driver'
left join ng_public.fleet_company fc on fc.id = fd.company_id 
left join ng_public.invoicing_fee_calculator ifc on ifc.company_id = fc.id 
	and ifc.start_date <= etl.created_date 
	and coalesce(ifc.end_date, DATE('9999-01-01')) > etl.created_date 
	and ifc.is_active = true
where etl.created >= DATE('2023-09-01') -- define time period start here
and etl.created < DATE('2023-10-01') -- define time period end here
and ifc.invoicing_strategy = 'company' -- fleets only / company based invoicing right
and fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code != fc.vat_code -- VAT code on the driver profile do not match with VAT code on the company profile
and etl.from_vat_code = fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code -- VAT code on the ride invoice matches with VAT code on the driver profile
)
select 
country,
count(*) as count_invoices
from summary
group by 1{noformat}

+Box answer:+ This cannot be deleted - no SaaS provider can warrant this. Box warrants how it provides its service but cannot warrant outcomes which are not entirely in Box’s control. Box customers are presumably selecting Box because of its robust security infrastructure and because it is a more economical approach than on premise solutions. Access to the service can be disrupted, and content can be destroyed or lost for reasons unrelated to Box’s performance. For example, Content can be lost if it is uploaded during a network interruption on a Customer network or stolen if a user shares a password or leaves a laptop open in public. What Box provides is robust technical and security procedures to prevent theft or destruction of Content, more information about which can be found in the Security Exhibit and our Audit Reports.

 

*_Section 11_* _- There is no termination for convenience. We suggest the addition of a clause for termination without a cause with 3 months notice._

+Box answer:+ This cannot be added to the BSA. Termination for convenience is not provided on deals as it negates the certainty of the deal and leads to revenue recognition problems. Additionally, the pricing provided to customers is predicated on their commitment to the specified term.

h3. {color:#36b37e}The logic of the breakdown of “overcharge” processes {color}([Figma|https://www.figma.com/file/VrgwCZuXPFcZpsEzlwEaQS/%F0%9F%9A%97-Rider-complains-about-an-overcharge?type=whiteboard&node-id=0-1&t=66rniRot3i7lpaAb-0])

* When the user contacts CS and *mentions the reason* for the overcharge (e.g. why do I have to pay more if the driver selected a longer route), or the reason is clear from a first glance at the ticket/order, CS will go straight to the relevant article by the issue type (in this case - “Rider complains driver took a longer route”).
* When the user contacts CS with a general complaint about an overcharge, and they *don’t know the reason*, CS should follow the “Rider complains about an overcharge” article. Any other articles for overcharges are related to specific situations, and this one is the only “general” article when the overcharge reason is unknown yet.

||*Overcharge cause is known*||*Overcharge cause is unknown yet*||
|[🚗 Rider reports they were charged additional fees|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/115003268153]|[🚗 Rider complains about an overcharge|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012406780]|
|[🚗 Rider reports driver did not end or start trip correctly|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010093954]| |
|[🚗 Rider reports driver did not arrive at correct pickup location|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013977839]| |
|[🚗 Rider did not get to the destination|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013967819]| |
|[🚗 User unhappy with a completed Price Review|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/360013392319]| |
|[🚗 Rider reports they were charged cancellation fee|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012407420]| |
|[🚗 Rider complains driver took a longer route|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012505659]| |
|[🚗 Rider reports driver made additional stops|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005970180]| |

* When the overcharge reason is unknown from the first customer contact and CS follows the “Rider complains about an overcharge” article, it can happen that *during the investigation it turns out that it’s a longer route or any other issue* that is covered in the dedicated article. In that case, CS should switch to that dedicated process.
* When I spoke to TLs and CS agents and asked them if there are any missing scenarios in “Rider complains about an overcharge” article, all of them mentioned *situations that are already covered in their dedicated articles*. It shows that when dealing with overcharges, people will first check the “Rider complains about an overcharge” article, rather than searching for a dedicated article by the issue type.
* *Since the “Rider complains about an overcharge” article seems to be the main source of information for CS when dealing with overcharges, and since it is quite hard for agents to understand which process to follow, I would like to build the “Rider complains about an overcharge” article like this:*
** Investigation part
** Choose the relevant process based on your findings:
*** [🚗 Rider reports they were charged additional fee|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/115003268153]
*** [🚗 Rider reports driver did not arrive at correct pickup location|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013977839]
*** All other overcharge articles
** If the overcharge is caused because of GPS/network issues, traffic on a suggested road, or by rider selecting the wrong destination, continue to the relevant section _(in this article)_:
*** GPS
*** Traffic
*** Wrong destination

h3. {color:#36b37e}“Rider complains about an overcharge” main changes{color}

* *Automation check:* currently every scenario starts with exactly the same action related to automation (if automation applied - inform the customer, if not - further actions), and it’s repeated in every scenario. To simplify, shorten the process, and avoid repetitive information, automation check actions are added before the article is split into scenarios.
* *GPS/Network issues:* Nigeria-specific instructions were removed.
* *Traffic problems:* Action to give goodwill compensation is removed. It's better to educate customers about our pricing process, preventing fixed price expectations. Traffic is an everyday issue and if we will compensate for that, customers will take advantage. Long-term, this isn't a good solution. And traffic is not something that we should take responsibility for.
* *Driver went to incorrect destination:* scenario is removed. We have 2 processes that are related to this - _🚗 Rider reports driver did not end or start trip correctly_ (for situations when driver did not end the ride) and _🚗 Rider did not get to the destination_ (when driver did not get to their destination or *went to the wrong destination*). Both processes have the same compensation action. So we definitely don't need to have this scenario here too, as a 3rd process.
* *Driver asked for more money on cash campaign trip* will be created as a separate article, to bring more clarity and make it easier for agents to follow processes. 
** All investigation actions in the article are not related to this scenario (checking the map, the surge, the destination..).
** Automations are not available in cash orders, so the automation part is also not relevant for this scenario.
** This is the only scenario related to BQS (it has the following actions). The other 3 scenarios are not related to BQS and they end either with compensation or informing R that automation applied. I think one of the main confusion factors is when we have 1 article for multiple scenarios with completely different endings. 
* *Actioning the report:* Market-specific instructions for Ghana and Ireland were removed, leaving the article only with Global actions.

h3. {color:#36b37e}Cleaning fee & User unhappy with a completed Price Review{color}

* The cleaning fee process is only for those markets where *the fee is added to the final price* through Price Review.
* There are *10* such markets (and for the remaining 20 this process is not applicable).
* Since the process itself basically has *no actions and no value*, there is no need to have it as a separate article. The process can be *merged with “User unhappy with a completed PR”* because it is actually about the user being unhappy that the cleaning fee was added to the price through PR. 
* I kept the only 1 action, which is to inform the rider that the cleaning fee was added. *I removed the part where the user thinks they were incorrectly charged, because:*
** I spoke to TLs of markets where the fee is added to the price, they confirmed that these situations *rarely occur*.
** We have a detailed [process|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360003076474] that must be followed before adding the cleaning fee to the price. CS must confirm a lot of things, which leaves basically *no room for error* (incorrectly added cleaning fee). In some markets, the driver even needs to agree with the rider after the ride, that the fee will be charged.
** If CS follows the mentioned process, confirms that the rider did indeed made a mess in the driver's vehicle, and agrees with the driver that the cleaning fee should be compensated, but then receives a different story from the rider and chooses to believe the rider's version, it will result "*he-said-she-said*" situations and will create even more confusion and additional customer contacts, as the driver will be left confused why the earlier agreed cleaning fee was taken away. 

[*🚗 Rider reports they were charged cleaning fee*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360017763659] *→ To be archived*

[*🚗 User unhappy with a completed Price Review*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013392319] *→ Cleaning fee part to be added (*[*Figma*|https://www.figma.com/file/Kc3Mi9fKhtfpiCCFEkXXOk/%F0%9F%9A%97-User-unhappy-with-a-completed-Price-Review?type=whiteboard&node-id=0-1&t=eoB5OoY5oSM4JxQr-0] *model)*

*** If the number in the PO number field in Telema is a Workday Purchase Order, then the Supplier Invoice will be linked (current logic).
*** If the number in the PO number field in Telema is *not* a Workday Purchase Order, then the Supplier Invoice will have this number filled into the “External Purchase Order” field.

{panel}

* External Purchase Order
** An invoice in Telema with no Purchase Order at all (empty field).
** An invoice in Telema with a *valid* Workday Purchase Order, for EE003.
** An invoice in Telema with an *invalid* Workday Purchase Order, for EE003.
** An invoice in Telema with a *valid* Workday Purchase Order, for any other company.
** An invoice in Telema with an *invalid* Workday Purchase Order Number, for any other company

These errors are caused by spikes in the number of calls to {{/internal/getProfile}}, from {{delivery_courier}}, which can’t handle that many calls at once. The spike happens from time to time, when we send a set of high surge notifications to couriers.

As per [this Slack thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02BXQA9GNS/p1698235342737919], we have decided to reduce the batch size of the high surge push notification calls. It is currently set at 100.

An alternative solution would have been to reduce the concurrency level with which the push notifications are sent (currently set at 3). However, we do not know what side effects it could produce for other notifications types, and reducing it to 2 might not even solve this problem completely. For this reason, we decided to reduce the batch size instead.

The task to reduce the batch size is [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CE-380].

You may close this ticket. 

Just so you know, these communications happen when the business user contacts us directly (through the App or e-mail), asking the reason why they can’t order with their business payment method. 

They can’t order because of the fraud trigger that prevents users from creating multiple business accounts without paying their debts. If a user is connected to a company that has debt, even if they were removed from the company, they will still be affected by it and will be unable to order with the business. This type of case isn’t very common and usually only affects people who are actually trying to commit fraud.

We have set that:

* If the company looks legit and the business user isn’t fraudulent >> I will escalate the case to the Fraud team to analyse the account and remove the block in the user’s profile;
* If the company looks fraudulent, I will just inform the user that their business payment method has been removed due to irregular activities (and don’t provide additional context). 



Sorry for taking your time. If you still want to know more information on the subject, please let me know.

Thank you!

I just got a reply from [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], Product Legal, who informed that the Product and Dev-Compliance team are still working on making this feature fully compliant. Unfortunately, the development does not move as quickly as we want it to move.

*The Driver Selfie Verification Feature is not fully compliant with the P2B Regulation yet*

Apparently we do not yet have the systems in place for the feature to work in a way that is fully compliant with the Platform-to-business Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 (often referred to as the P2B Regulation). The compliance issues relate to screen copies and emails. The wording on the screenshots shown to the drivers is unclear, and there are no emails sent out to drivers in the event that they are blocked due to failed selfie verification, therefore the feature does not meet the requirements set on a online intermediation service, i.e. an online platform, such as Bolt, under the P2B Regulation. 

*The risks of rolling out this feature even though it’s not fully compliant yet*  

Non-compliance with the P2B Regulation can lead to Bolt becoming subject to a prohibition procedure before the Finnish Market Court. Such procedures can be initiated by another company or their representative organisations. If the procedure, e.g., for the Driver Selfie Verification-feature, used by Bolt is deemed non-compliant by the Market Court, the Market Court can prohibit Bolt from continuing to use that procedure and may combine the prohibition with an obligation for Bolt to pay a financial penalty. 

In addition, a company may raise civil claims about the same procedure before a district court, and if it’s been established by the Market Court that the procedure is not compliant with the P2B Regulation, the claimant’s chances of winning the case against Bolt may increase.

*Should we roll out or wait, and what is the timeline?*

Please consider the risks of rolling out this feature even though it’s not fully compliant yet. If you wish to take the risk and still want roll out the feature before it can be fully compliant, then we can proceed to finalise the T&Cs (linked in my last comment) and draft comms. In that case, we can have the comms published, _at the earliest,_ end of next week, and the T&Cs will start to apply from middle/end of November, whereafter the feature can be launched in Finland. But if you would not like to take the risk, then it will unfortunately take longer before the feature can be rolled out.

Please let us know how you wish to proceed, and please do not hesitate to ask if you have any questions.

Best regards,

Ida

Hello [~accountid:5e620d95ed743a0afe39736b] ,

Before sharing the doc with the suggestions, I would like to know what you think about the following topics and if you agree with the conclusion:



Both agreements are very different in the sense that one outlines rights and obligations between Bolt and Axxicom while the other one outlines rights and obligations between Bolt Drivers and Axxicom.

Since the drivers are self-employed and not employees of the company, we shouldn’t assume responsibilities as if they were Bolt’s dependents and try to detach the company as much as possible from the agreement “*STOBA Regeling Chauffeurs*”.



Taking into account that drivers are not under Bolt’s control and supervision, in “*AGREEMENT ON AXXICOM AND BOLT FOR USE OF OPERATIONAL LAYER AND P41*”, we should not: 

* assume responsibility for drivers acts and omissions, 
* ensure that drivers comply with regulations, 
* ensure that  drivers agree with conditions of the airport’s regulations
* pay fines for drivers' acts and omissions as mentioned in section 7.

* assume the obligations in 6.2; 6.3; 6.4; 6.5. 
* assume liability and indemnity for drivers acts/omissions (8.1)

On the contrary, I believe that, if anyone is to assume these responsibilities and obligations, that should be the drivers themselves in their own agreements with Axxicom (“*Stoba Regeling Chauffeurs*”).

With respect to Axxicom’s disclaimer clause 8.2, it is not reasonable so I would like to cross it out. Moreover, we cannot agree to this clause on driver’s behalf.



Regarding *Stoba Regeling Chauffeurs,* I have the following questions:

* From an operational point of view, do you see a possible way in which drivers can consent to *Stoba Regeling Chauffeurs* autonomously?
* From an operational point of view, do you find possible drivers issuing their smartcards autonomously with Axxicom without Bolt’s involvement?
* Is Bolt sharing drivers’ data with Axxicom? If yes, which data?
* What data about the drivers would the smartcards be containing? Are drivers providing the data by themselves with Axxicom? Do we have any involvement in that process?

Other than that, in *Stoba Regeling Chauffeurs*, as drivers should be able to decide autonomously whether to agree or not with it, I don’t have more concerns from a legal perspective. 



In conclusion, I would like to counter-propose withdrawing the mentioned obligations from *AGREEMENT ON AXXICOM AND BOLT FOR USE OF OPERATIONAL LAYER AND P41* and, if necessary, transfer them to *Stoba Regeling Chauffeurs* so that drivers take the responsibility from their own actions/omissions.

Please, let me know if you agree with this line of thinking and if it's feasible from an operational point of view.

From this driver deducts WTH

In various countries, the service fees paid for Bolt services are subject to withholding tax (hereinafter also ‘WHT’). This means that the recipient of Bolt’s platform service is obliged, under local regulations, to pay the fees net of the withholding tax (the WHT is effectively tax on Bolt) and to report and transfer the respective withholding tax themselves to the local tax authority.

Provided the service fee is set-off automatically in our settlement system without accounting for withholding tax, this creates the situation where often the service recipients cannot fulfill their obligations. Consequently, in the settlement system, the set-off should take place net of the withholding tax.

+*ROMANIA*+



2% withholding tax applies to the commission fees invoiced by Bolt to the fleets.



In the settlement system, we should take into account the we should collect from the clients the service fees minus the withholding tax i.e. the set-off should take place net of the withholding tax and indicate it clearly on the settlement document as “compensation for withholding tax”.



_Example: Rider pays the fleet 1000 fees for a ride, which is collected by Bolt. Bolt issues a service fee invoice to the driver for 100 (e.g. 10% of the payment). Withholding tax is 2%. Bolt transfers to the restaurant 902 (fees 1000 - commission 100 + wht 2)._

Hi here is the comment from the TAX regarding the invoices that have been reissued in OCT (what we are still checking this possibility)

regarding the deductibility of the VAT we are paying and not requesting refund from the fleets, the tax authorities can try to argue that the VAT on this invoice is not deductible because of the wrong issuance date. However, after checking decisions from the European Court of Justice on the right to deduct VAT included in incorrect invoices, I note that there are court cases that refer that the tax authorities cannot refuse the deduction of VAT solely on the grounds that a formal requirement of the invoice is not met, as long as they have information to verify whether the substantive conditions for the deduction are complied with (e.g., the transactions took place, the input VAT referred to services acquired to perform VAT taxable transactions such as the transport services) and said information may be produced by the taxpayers. Moreover, these cases address the question of the description of the services in the invoices because the tax authorities could not verify what services were provided. In this context, I understand that the wrong issuance date is not an issue that should restrict the right to deduct VAT and it should not jeopardise the right of the fleets deducting the VAT. In any case, as pointed out by [@izabela.potega|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U04C883QJ20] they are not incurring in any additional costs with the new invoices and therefore if they or their accounting / tax advisors are not comfortable with the deduction, they should not do it.

h3. {color:#36b37e}The name of the article{color}

Following up on my idea in the previous note, that the [+🚗 Rider complains about an overcharge+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012406780] article is a primary source of information when dealing with overcharges, and sometimes CS mistakenly choose this article, when there is actually another one, dedicated to the specific overcharge issue, I think it would make sense to rename it.

All the articles about specific situations start with “Rider complains/Rider reports”, and that makes sense because we know exactly what the Rider is reporting and that is reflected in the name of the article. But for the “Rider complains about an overcharge”, the overcharge reason is unknown and the article is dedicated to *finding out what caused the overcharge*. So I think it would make sense to change the name “Rider complains about an overcharge” to *“Identifying overcharge cause”*. 

The current name can be a bit misleading and say that if there’s an overcharge, this is the process to follow. When in reality, if there is an overcharge and the cause is known - the dedicated process needs to be followed. And if the cause is unknown - then the “Identifying overcharge cause” article should be followed.

This also aligns with the Supportability team’s logic, as Mariia said: “_I was charged more than expected_ should be used when they claim that the price seems unfair and doesn’t match the initial estimated, when they don’t assume why exactly it happened. While _My driver took a poor route_ should appear only in the tickets where riders directly complained about the bad route drivers chose”.

*Further to our last update, please be informed that we were at the NIC, Lagos, today October 24, 2023, for the abovementioned suit, which came up for ruling and judgement. We have summarized the Ruling of the Preliminary Objection and the Judgement below.*

 

*OUR PRELIMINARY OBJECTION.*

 

*You may recall that we filed a preliminary objection wherein we submitted two issues to be determined:-*

# *_Whether the National Industrial Court lacks subject matter jurisdiction to hear and determine this suit as presently constituted?_*
# *_In the event that issue 1 is resolved against the Applicants, whether this Honourable Court ought to strike out the names of the 2_*^*_nd_*^ *_3_*^*_rd_*^ *_and 4_*^*_th_*^ *_Applicants from this suit?_*

 

*Regarding the first issue, the judge in her ruling held that it had jurisdiction to hear the suit as The National Industrial Court (NIC)  rules provides that an applicant may institute a suit by any one of the acceptable methods and was therefore not limited to instituting its claim by way of a “Compliant”.  The Court further stated that the form in which the Claimant lodged its suit was proper and therefore on that bases assumed jurisdiction to hear its claim.*

 

*Regarding the second issue, the Court held that the 2*^*nd*^ *Respondent/Defendant (Bolt Technology OU) was a co -employer of the Applicant and therefore a necessary party to the suit. The Court however stated that the 3*^*rd*^ *and 4*^*th*^ *Respondents/ Defendants were acting as agents to the 1*^*st*^ *Defendant not in their personal capacity and thereby were not necessary parties to the suit and therefore struck both parties out of the suit.*

 

*THE SUBSTANSIVE SUIT.*

 

*The Judge in rejecting the claimant claim held that she did not show sufficient evidence to buttress her allegations regarding termination of her employment due discrimination. The Learned Justice also held that the Claimant did not show sufficient evidence entitling her receiving medical expenses from the Defendants and was therefore not entitled to same.*  

 

*The Court however granted the Claimant N5,000,000.00 ( Five Million Naira ) as general damages for wrongful termination by the Defendant on the bases that the 1*^*st*^ *Defendant did not give valid reason why it had terminated the Claimants Contract of Employment.  The Court also awarded the Claimant the sum of N1,000,000 ( One Million Naira)  as cost of the legal action and ordered that the sums be paid within one month of the Judgment after which interest will begin to accrue.*

 

*NEXT STEPS*

 

*We have seen that most judges of the NICN disregard the common law position that an Employer can terminate without giving reason and instead insist that employers must adhere to terminating with reason as this is “international best practice”. However, many decisions similar to ours where the NICN has held that employers must terminate with reason have been upturned by the Court of Appeal, with the most recent judgement delivered on the 27*^*th*^ *of June 2023 in LIGHTENING NETWORKS LIMITED V AUTA NYADA AND ORS, where the superior court in allowing the appeal held that it is settled law that an employer has the unfettered right to terminate the employees employment and is not bound to give reasons for the termination of the said employment. He may terminate for Good or Bad reason or no reason at all.*  

 

*We have applied for the CTC of the Judgement and will share same as soon as we receive a copy. Flowing from the above, it is our recommendation that this part of the Judgement be appealed and look forward to receiving your instructions.*

It might be possible due to a day-end ride/bonuses/compensations, usually, the orders finished at midnight are added to the next day’s balance, as the balance calculation is based on the time stamp.

This causes a time difference between the payout system and the balance system. However, the balance and the payout is correct. It is only a discrepancy in the reporting. Most importantly they have received this difference in the next payout.

Please check the [new view|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/balance?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_date_ts%22%3A1697407200%2C%22end_date_ts%22%3A1698012000%2C%22types%22%3A%5B%22ride_hailing_fleet%22%5D%2C%22external_id%22%3A56086%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] balance to check the correctness of the payout.( as the source of truth)

And please check [the record|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/records?recordFilter=%7B%22action_timestamp_from%22%3A1697407200%2C%22action_timestamp_to%22%3A1698012000%2C%22from_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22from_agent_id%22%3A56086%2C%22agent_filter_operator%22%3A%22OR%22%2C%22to_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22to_agent_id%22%3A56086%7D&page=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%2C%22offset%22%3A0%7D] of the end days of Sunday (in this example will be a different timezone because of my location)

This is what the Legal Department of the police writes:

There is no express provision stating that the Police Authority may request information, but according to ch. 23 Section 4 of the Code of Procedure RB, the investigation must be conducted objectively and take into account and take into account circumstances and evidence that speak both to the suspect's advantage and to his or her disadvantage. Furthermore, the police must search for and actively strive to enrich the preliminary investigation material with things that can help the investigation forward.

The FU leader is responsible for the case and must take the measures necessary to investigate the crime. One such action could be to request a document. In this sense, the police do not have a provision that says that we may request, but rather that we have an obligation to do so (ch. 23 § 4 RB).

If the individual does not want to hand over the material, the FU leader has the opportunity to make formal decisions and use the criminal procedural coercive means available in RB such as house search and seizure to obtain the requested material. Such possibilities do exist, but such a procedure tends to take more time from the owner of the property, to ultimately lead to the same result, i.e. that the police may take part in requested material.

See also attached information sheet about GDPR.

Hey [~accountid:6140b8db805a97006aa66cc8] / [~accountid:5d5a47614aeeb80c2cc0d00a] 

We have now received advice from external counsel on the proposed adverts. Please see below: 

* Providing the claims that are made in the adverts are accurate and can be evidenced, these would not fall foul of the misleading advertising rules. In order to ensure compliance with the rules on comparative advertising, the information on which the comparison is based would need to  be included in the advert, this is to allow customers to verify this information. This would be sufficient to link to a webpage with this information (as opposed to detailing the information in full in the advert).



* External counsel have recommended to reduce the 18% figure to 15% for “additional earnings with Bolt” for the comparison with companies taking 15% commission, this is to ensure that the % increase presented is as accurate as possible and is rounded down rather than rounded up to overstate Bolt’s position.

+*_The key compliance issues you should be aware of are:_*+

*Accuracy* - providing the claims made in the adverts are accurate, and no key information is excluded, they will comply with the rules on misleading advertising. A concern would arise if the information was being presented in a way that could be considered deceptive, or if the comparisons made were not fair, reasonable and accurate. 

*Clarity* - when making the comparison included within both advertisements, you must ensure that the basis of the comparison is clear and that you have clearly and unambiguously stated what the financial comparison is. External counsel in their view believe this has been achieved, however that is subject to the change detailed above regarding the figure of 18% increase in drier earnings as against a company taking 15% commission.

*Evidence* - There are additional requirements regarding the evidence you have in support of the statements made in the advert. Prior to publication of the adverts, you should ensure that you hold documentary evidence that shows the comparisons made are accurate, fair and reasonable, and that they provide the accuracy of the data and statistics that you are relying on. In addition you are also required to hold documentary evidence to demonstrated that you have checked that the competitor’s prices quoted are accurate and up to date. This will likely be documentation that you have already obtained in order to create the ad. It is imperative to hold this evidence on file this is because if any questions were raised around the accuracy of the claims.

*Verification* - whilst the adverts do not mention any competitor by name, the likely competitors to whom the comparisons are being made are fairly easily identifiable. This brings the adverts within the scope of the requirement to make the comparisons verifiable. The adverts should direct consumers to sufficient information to allow them to understand the comparison and check the claim is accurate. This can be achieved either by including a link to the source where you have drawn the statistics from, or perhaps for feasible to a webpage on Bolts own site where full information on the comparison would be provided. Alternatively you can provide a postal or email address where consumers can contact you to obtain the information.

+*_Risks / penalties for not complying with the rules_*+

# If the adverts were to be found to be in breach of the rules outlined above, the first level of sanction would likely be an investigation by the Advertising Standards Authority and a request from them to have the advert removed or revised.
# Tougher sanctions that can be applied where a complaint is made directly to Trading Standards, or where an ASA sanction is not complied with, and in addition individuals who enter into contracts with Bolt as a result of the adverts might have a right to civil redress if they consider the claims to be inaccurate.
# Most extreme sanctions, offences under the legislation governing misleading and comparative advertising can result in unlimited fines or up to two years imprisonment.

{color:#ff5630}*NOTE:*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}The greater the volume of documentation available to substantiate any claims made, the better the defence is for any such allegation.

+*SUMMARY*+

[~accountid:6140b8db805a97006aa66cc8] / [~accountid:5d5a47614aeeb80c2cc0d00a] 

* Please ensure that the underlying data supporting this comparison has been assessed and reviewed in full and checked that all data supporting the comparisons are up-to-date.



* Ensure the claims made in the adverts are accurate and can be evidenced. We would suggest gathering all the evidence you are relying on and safely store this in a folder, this will help mitigate any potential questions if they were raised.



* We would suggest amending the advert as per counsels recommendation to reduce the 18% figure to 15% for “additional earnings with Bolt”.



* As highlight by counsel this advert is verifiable therefore please adopt the suggested approach of either including a link to the source of where the statistics have been drawn from (when making comparisons to competitors) or incorporate these on Bolts own website providing full information. Alternatively, provide a postal or email address so consumers can contact Bolt to obtain the information

Hi [~accountid:5fc110f70d2f61006f7604a9] 

Thank you for the clarification. Please find my assessment of the issue from a legal perspective below.

*Summary of legal assessment*

The user may choose to end the contract with Bolt, but the user does not have any legal right to a refund due to withdrawal in accordance with the Swedish consumer protection legislation. Nevertheless, I understand that we do offer refunds even though the user may not necessarily be _legally_ entitled to it. Any such refund would be a commercial decision rather than a legal one. Against this background, please choose yourself whether or not you choose to refund the user for the trip, e.g. based on CS principles / routines. 

Please see further details on the legal side of things below.

*The user’s request to withdraw from the contract*

Regarding the user’s request to withdraw from the contract with Bolt, the user is free to _end the contract_ with us. However, for rentals, as a rule, users have no right to “withdraw” from the contract with Bolt, except for in relation to pre-paid passes that have not yet been activated. The same applies under Swedish consumer protection law as well as our T&Cs ([+Terms of Service for Bolt E-Vehicles in Sweden, link+|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/lxZLg2GyvPx4Q04XdX8Gl/bc265559c9bb974194e41fdcdd073e9b/SE_Bolt_E-Vehicles_T_Cs__v_20230201_in_English_.docx.pdf]).

Please note that there is an exception to the aforementioned, which applies *if the user has purchased a pre-paid pass*. This is the only situation when the user has a withdrawal right according to Swedish consumer legislation as well as our T&Cs. Please see section 5.3. of the [+T&Cs+|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/lxZLg2GyvPx4Q04XdX8Gl/bc265559c9bb974194e41fdcdd073e9b/SE_Bolt_E-Vehicles_T_Cs__v_20230201_in_English_.docx.pdf] (I have also +attached+ a screenshot of the relevant clause for your reference). _Provided that the user has not purchased any pre-paid pass_, the only way the user is entitled to “withdraw” from the contract with Bolt in this case is basically by deleting the app / stop using our services. As already mentioned above, this does however _not_ entitle the user to any refund on any _legal basis_.

Please let me know if you have any further questions on the legal aspects of this issue, or if we can close the ticket.

Best regards,

Ida

h3. {color:#36b37e}Compensation logic in all processes{color}

I reviewed the compensation part in every Rider process and documented it [*here*|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1wX8Z54jhSgbKobrT6oOGmEq-ybqmWJPpxwESjfnmMg0/edit#gid=975222474]*.* Changes that I made:

* [*🚗 Rider complains about rude driver*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/360012052520] - this was the only quality/driver behavior complaint that had no compensation. It didn’t make sense, because in other similar cases (bad driver’s appearance, poor vehicle condition, etc) we offer a small sum compensation to BB. So I added the same compensation to this process as well.
* [*🚗 Rider reports that driver asked for money upfront*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013847139] - this process was wrong, as it is only for cash orders, but the compensation action was to refund to BB. I changed it to promo codes. 
* I removed from ~6 processes the part that said “if the overcharge is double, issue a full refund to the original payment method”, as per agreement with Commerce. 

Besides these changes that I made, the compensation part in all processes looks logical. We don’t have different actions and they are more or less aligned across processes - if it’s an overcharge, the overcharged amount is refunded to BB, and if it’s a complaint, then the small sum compensation to BB is offered (promo code in cash orders). And if the case is related to a cancellation/wait time fee, the fee is refunded to BB.

** getOrderDetails is called in almost all cases for event handlers
** we could make a versions for each actor as Provider/Courier events don’t have the same necessities
** also the OrderDetails object is used to get information in many places throughout Timing with various needs
** this would also mean that we could request less entities per specific call to order mall

Yes, checking the score like previously is outdated as there is no ‘refresh’ to the score without a customer attempting to place another order. 

The important part here is to review if the customer is verified successfully and, if so, advise them to try again. Verification is the recovery process for good users and, hence, if the verification has failed or the customer does not get offered one (where the automatic process is live), we can follow the ‘this is an irregular user' flow.

The calculation can be checked to confirm if the user is passing after verification or not, but it means that the customer will need to retry after verification for us to see the attempt result and any blockers. 

Cheers,

Hi [~accountid:5d8df399c7d4e30dc2836580] 

Product legal have now provided further insight into this category and whether or not a T&C update is required. Please see below: 

* In most of the markets that this category is live the drivers acquire the car seat. 
* In some other markets there is a plan for Bolt to acquire the car seats, however this has not undergone a legal assessment yet.

*_T&Cs_*

* Currently there is no mention of this category in the Driver or Passengers T&Cs .

*_Disclaimers_*

* There is no disclaimer in the app for when a rider selects this category (in case the car seat is not suitable/incorrect size or type of car seat for the child).

*_Who is responsible for the safety of the car seat_*

There are strict rules imposed on child seat safety in the EU and the UK. For example: if there is a road traffic accident the car seat cannot be used anymore and needs to be changed. Therefore, Bolt would need to ensure that the driver maintains the safety of the car seat instead of Bolt assuming this responsibility. 

+*Summary*+

* If this new category is rolled out in the UK there would need to be an update to the current Driver T&Cs and the Passenger T&Cs.
* We would have to conduct further analysis on any reclassification risks. One of the potential risks here is, if Bolt requests the driver maintains the safety of the seat and puts this requirement on the driver (whether this is imposed by wording in the T&Cs or otherwise), this may be construed as a method of ‘control’. 
* If you intend on only one child seat type/size, we would suggest having a disclaimer for situations where a rider may select this category but when the driver turns up this is not the correct seat size for the child. The disclaimer could potentially be added to the passenger T&Cs. 

Please reach out to me on slack if you want to discuss further. 

Thank you

*_Please see my review below:_*

*Clause 1* - there is no real change here, the drafting has just been made clearer,  this amendment is fine. 

*Clause 4 -*  there has been a slight change as the word ‘reasonable’ has been added, his amendment is fine. 

*Clause 5 (b) -* I can see they have changed the interest rate basis to the Bank of England whereas it used to be Barclays Bank plc, this amendment is fine. 

*Clause 5 (i)* - amendment is more beneficial to Bolt, as the licensor now has to give Bolt 24 hours notice to enter the space (with the exception of emergencies) whereas no notice was required before. This amendment is fine. 

*Clause 11 (a)* - There is no real change here, the drafting has been made clearer. Bolt still has the right to terminate the licence agreement with +no less than 3 months+ notice - which means Bolt can still get out of the agreement quickly if needed. This amendment is fine. 

*Clause 11 (c)* -  the wording here is now more beneficial to Bolt as the licensor is now giving Bolt one months notice as opposed to one weeks notice in writing to terminate,  this amendment is fine. 

*Clause 15* -the licensor has to now give Bolt one month before disposing of any items left at the premises, whereas this used to be one week. This is more beneficial to Bolt, this amendment is fine. 

+*To summarise*+

Update: Discussed with [~accountid:63622e9d548f1fe6f0c7befd] and [~accountid:630f17fc8d88ec800fbe4799] . Currently, all other entities except for {{courier}} send their {{entity_id}} when they send tin validation requests to billing side. Billing side then stores this information as {{local_id}} and is is then possible to retrieve it from billing side & create links to profiles in TIN Validation page of admin-panel. However, we found out that {{courier}} does not follow this logic, probably due to the initial system where leads were used as the place to perform TIN validation. For {{courier}} validation, we send as {{local_id}} the {{tin_validation_id}} we use in our {{tin_validation}} table. Therefore it is non-straightforward to create the courier profile links in TIN Validation page.

Possible solutions:

* Create a separate endpoint in {{courier-validation}}: We will receive {{local_id}}s and return their mapped {{courier_id}}s, allowing us to generate the links. However it will require 2 api calls and might add extra complexity to TIN Validation page
* Add redirection logic in TIN Validation page: We will render {{courier-validation}} links with {{local id}}s. They will be pointing to some redirection page, which will take the {{local_id}}, get {{courier_id}}, construct the URL and redirect to the courier profile. However, not sure how long it will take to implement, and may still require additional endpoint. It will reduce the number of calls required though
* Make courier validation logic consistent with other entities: Modify courier creation to send {{courier_id}} as {{local_id}}. Will be the most complex development work within all of the discussed solutions, since it will require refactoring {{validateCourierTaxDetails}} and {{updateCourierTaxDetails}} endpoints, how they are called and the whole courier creation flow, as well as possibly breaking a large number of tests. It will also require additional backfilling. However, it will be the best solution as it will end up simplifying our courier creation logic as well as keeping everything consistent with the other entities.

Task is blocked pending the decision on which solution to use & how to implement it

In this case you can follow the [kb|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/9406080396178#user-cannot-reserve-a-vehicleorder-a-trip-due-to-negative-bolt-balance].
User cannot reserve a vehicle/order a trip due to negative Bolt Balance

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [Transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [User page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.


If you require any further information, let me know.Best Regards,

*Mozilla DeepSpeech*

* Streaming Interface - Yes
* Pre-trained model is only for English
* Tools to train own model are available
* Supported platforms:
** Linux/AMD64
** Linux/ARMv7
** Linux/Aarch64 (Cortex-A72)
** MacOS/AMD64 (there is no support of M1)
** Windows/AMD64
** Android/ARMv7
** Android/Aarch64
* API bindings for:
** C
** Java
** JS (Node.js)
** Python

Comment: 

Mozilla DeepSpeech provides a bunch of tools for training own ASR (automatic speech recognition) models and to play them, however the supported platforms are quite outdated (the project is not developing for more than 2 years already) and it would be very much effortful from our side to keep this project running on modern platforms that we my need to support (eg. Android ARMv8a, Android ARM64 or MacOS M1 or adding support for iOS if we decided to support on-device offline speech-to-text transcription)

----

Coqui-STT

* Most likely that initially this project started as a fork of Mozilla DeepSpeech (resemblance of the API, documentation and supported platforms speaks for it).
* Coqui-STT maintainers deprecated the engine in favor of OpenAI Whisper.
* Pre-trained language models are not available anymore.
* Tools to train own model are available.
* Supported platforms:
** Linux/AMD64
** Linux/ARMv7
** Linux/Aarch64 (Cortex-A72)
** MacOS/AMD64 (there is no support of M1)
** Windows/AMD64
** Android/ARMv7
** Android/Aarch64
* API bindings for:
** C
** Java
** JS (Node.js, WASM)
** Python

Comment:

Coqui-STT project most likely is a fork of Mozilla DeepSpeech (though it’s not stated clearly anywhere in the documentation), hence all platform limitations stated for Mozilla DeepSpeech are relevant here as well. 

----

Bottomline:

Because the maintainers of Coqui-STT themselves suggest using OpenAI Whisper as a more up-to-date open source alternative for speech recognition, making a fork of any of these two STT engines in order to maintain them ourselves makes very little sense.

Took a quick look to help this issue move forward.

* Calculation inputs view uses a JS library called react-json-view
* The code it uses to render numerics is not configurable

⚠️ I also discovered that react-json-view is unmaintained since March 2021. It also contains an .innerHTML = assignment in copy/pasting that parses untrusted strings as HTML. This means we don’t have the luxury of upstreaming a feature to display N digits.

A cheap option is to simply convert all numerics to strings with toFixed(2) before passing to react-json-view, but this might be quite confusing as strings are quoted and have a different color.

An alternative is vendoring react-json-view into the repo and making the modifications in place.

A third option is to write a simplified version of react-json-view that aligns more precisely to the needs of input display.

The reverse charge mechanism is a tax regulation used in the European Union (EU) to account for Value Added Tax (VAT) in cross-border transactions between companies. In our scenario, where we are providing services in Malta but are not registered in Malta, and we're issuing invoices from an Estonian company with 0% VAT, the reverse charge mechanism would typically apply as follows:

*Service Provision:* we, as the Bolt company, provide services in Malta. Since we're not registered for VAT in Malta, we issue invoices from your Estonian company, Bolt Operations OÜ, with 0% VAT.
*Recipient in Malta:* The recipient of our services in Malta, assuming they are a registered VAT payer in Malta, is responsible for accounting for the VAT on our behalf. They will be the one to report and pay the VAT to the Maltese tax authorities.
*Reverse Charge Mechanism:* In a reverse charge situation, it is the responsibility of the recipient, not the supplier, to calculate and pay the VAT due on the transaction. The recipient will account for both the input VAT (VAT on the purchase) and the output VAT (VAT on the sale) on their VAT return. In this case, the recipient will calculate the VAT they would have paid if the services were provided by a Maltese supplier.
*Reporting:* The Maltese recipient of our services will report the reverse charge VAT on their VAT return. This ensures that the VAT revenue is collected in Malta, even though the supplier (our Estonian company) is not registered for VAT in Malta.

"_Dear Europ Assistance team, Thank you for your email. We hope all is well with you. With reference to the procedure in case the passenger transport is carried out outside the Czech Republic, we agree that pursuant to the applicable VAT framework, the transport is located in the Member State in which the transport takes place, being therefore subject to local VAT. In this context, whenever there are rides taken in a different Member State, such as the Polish rides included in invoice No. CZ1523-1305, Bolt pays for the invoices issued by drivers and requests a refund of costs to business customers, which should not be subject to VAT. In case the drivers or fleets established in different Member States issued documents directly to Europ Assistance, a VAT refund procedure would have to be initiated by Europ Assistance in the relevant Member States. Additionally, if Bolt used different VAT registrations to charge local VAT in each jurisdiction, it would not be possible to issue a single aggregated invoice to Europ Assistance as there would be multiple service providers for VAT purposes. In sum, this procedure allows Europ Assistance to avoid having to file refund requests to the tax authorities of different Member States while also receiving a single invoice for all services provided._ 

_Best regards_"

# No, Martin Villig has not been granted similar rights. How it's regulated in the Articles is by way of shareholding percentage, meaning that Markus, due to having considerably higher shareholding percentage has the right to ultimately appoint the management board members. 
# Simply looking at the provided "related party" definition, a person is deemed a related party in the following cases:
(i) has control or joint control of the company - Ahto does not have control over Bolt (not by way of shareholding percentage nor in any other way);
(ii) has significant influence over the reporting entity - Ahto does not have significant influence over Bolt, its operations or strategic decisions.
(iii) is a member of the key management personnel of the reporting entity or of a parent of the reporting entity - Ahto is not a member of Bolt's key management personnel. Again, we note that the definition refers to "key management personell" and does not make a reference to the management board of the company. However, we do note that Ahto is a member of the management board which, under the law, gives him the right to represent the company before third parties. If this (i.e. Ahto being on the management board) in your view deems him as someone who "is a member of key management personnel", then we can accept that (even though this is not our interpretation of the provided definition).
# The assessment with regard to Bolt Operations OÜ is the same as with regard to Bolt Technology OÜ. 
# Full list of related parties
*With regard to family members we note that IAS reads as follows: Close members of the family of a person are those family members who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, that person in their dealings with the entity and include.
Thus, IAS does not automatically assume that all close relatives are deemed related parties but only those who "may be expected to influence or be influenced" by that person [Markus, Jevgeni, Mikko, respectively] in their dealings with Bolt. This interpretation is also supported by the Interpretation Committee's paper ([https://www.ifrs.org/content/dam/ifrs/meetings/2015/january/ifrs-ic/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/ap13-definition-of-close-family-members.pdf)|https://www.ifrs.org/content/dam/ifrs/meetings/2015/january/ifrs-ic/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/ap13-definition-of-close-family-members.pdf)] which emphasises that the close family member criteria involves assessing the extent to which a close member is expected to influence or be influenced by a person, and that this assessment involves the use of judgement to determine on a case-by-case basis whether members of the family of a person (including that person’s parents) are related parties or not. Based on the foregoing, we find that only Martin Villig (co-founder of Bolt and brother of Markus Villig) fills that criteria and can be deemed as someone influencing or being influenced by Markus Villig (CEO of Bolt). 

* Markus Villig (control) - CEO
* Jevgeni Kabanov (key management)- President
* Mikko Salovaara (key management) - CFO
* Martin Villig (close family member) - co-founder/chairman of supervisory board

* The cleaning fee process is only for those markets where *the fee is added to the final price* through Price Review.

* I kept only 1 action, which is to inform the rider that the cleaning fee was added. *I removed the part where the user thinks they were incorrectly charged, because:*
** I spoke to TLs of markets where the fee is added to the price, they confirmed that these situations *rarely occur*.
** We have a detailed [process|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360003076474] that must be followed before adding the cleaning fee to the price. CS must confirm a lot of things, which leaves basically *no room for error* (incorrectly added cleaning fee). In some markets, the driver even needs to agree with the rider after the ride, that the fee will be charged.
** If CS follows the mentioned process, confirms that the rider did indeed made a mess in the driver's vehicle, and agrees with the driver that the cleaning fee should be compensated, but then receives a different story from the rider and chooses to believe the rider's version, it will result "*he-said-she-said*" situations and will create even more confusion and additional customer contacts, as the driver will be left confused why the earlier agreed cleaning fee was taken away.

h3. {color:#36b37e}“Rider complains about an overcharge” main changes ({color}[{color:#36b37e}Figma{color}|https://www.figma.com/file/VrgwCZuXPFcZpsEzlwEaQS/%F0%9F%9A%97-Rider-complains-about-an-overcharge?type=whiteboard&node-id=0-1&t=66rniRot3i7lpaAb-0]{color:#36b37e}){color}

* *Automation check:* currently every scenario starts with exactly the same action related to automation (if automation applied - inform the customer, if not - further actions), and it’s repeated in every scenario. To simplify, shorten the process, and avoid repetitive information, automation check actions are added before the article is split into scenarios.
* *GPS/Network issues:* Nigeria-specific instructions were removed.
* *Traffic problems:* Action to give goodwill compensation is removed. It's better to educate customers about our pricing process, preventing fixed price expectations. Traffic is an everyday issue and if we will compensate for that, customers will take advantage. Long-term, this isn't a good solution. And traffic is not something that we should take responsibility for.
* *Driver went to incorrect destination:* scenario is removed. We have 2 processes that are related to this - _🚗 Rider reports driver did not end or start trip correctly_ (for situations when driver did not end the ride) and _🚗 Rider did not get to the destination_ (when driver did not get to their destination or *went to the wrong destination*). Both processes have the same compensation action. So we definitely don't need to have this scenario here too, as a 3rd process.
* *Driver asked for more money on cash campaign trip* will be created as a separate article, to bring more clarity and make it easier for agents to follow processes.
** All investigation actions in the article are not related to this scenario (checking the map, the surge, the destination..).
** Automations are not available in cash orders, so the automation part is also not relevant for this scenario.
** This is the only scenario related to BQS (it has the following actions). The other 3 scenarios are not related to BQS and they end either with compensation or informing R that automation applied. I think one of the main confusion factors is when we have 1 article for multiple scenarios with completely different endings.
* *Actioning the report:* Market-specific instructions for Ghana and Ireland were removed, leaving the article only with Global actions.

h3. {color:#36b37e}The name of the article{color}

Following up on my idea in the previous note, that the [+🚗 Rider complains about an overcharge+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012406780] article is a primary source of information when dealing with overcharges, and sometimes CS mistakenly choose this article, when there is actually another one, dedicated to the specific overcharge issue, I think it would make sense to rename it.

All the articles about specific situations start with “Rider complains/Rider reports”, and that makes sense because we know exactly what the Rider is reporting and that is reflected in the name of the article. But for the “Rider complains about an overcharge”, the overcharge reason is unknown and the article is dedicated to *finding out what caused the overcharge*. So I think it would make sense to change the name “Rider complains about an overcharge” to *“Identifying overcharge cause”*.

The current name can be a bit misleading and say that if there’s an overcharge, this is the process to follow. When in reality, if there is an overcharge and the cause is known - the dedicated process needs to be followed. And if the cause is unknown - then the “Identifying overcharge cause” article should be followed.
