oh its not that easy: Redact Comment Attachment takes mandatory params:

{noformat}attachment_id	integer
comment_id	integer
ticket_id	integer{noformat}

whereas  {{zendesk_attachment_reupload}} has only columns:

{noformat}  `id` BIGINT UNSIGNED PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT COMMENT 'DataType:PKBID',
  `created` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `last_update` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `zendesk_ticket_id` INT(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  `attachment_url` VARCHAR(10000) NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  `failed_attempts` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `uploaded` TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,{noformat}

So in the step:

* _for each reuploaded non-deleted from zendesk call this_ [https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket-attachments/#redact-comment-attachment|https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/ticket-attachments/#redact-comment-attachment|smart-link] _and mark deletion status to 200 or 404 or 500 in table_

we need to get attachment_id and comment_id from zendesk_ticket_id and attachment_url. This is doable but non-trivial, we need to:
get all the events for a given zendesk_ticket_id from {{zendesk_ticket_event}} table. Then create a snapshot by 

{noformat}UserTicketSnapshot.create(ctx, zendeskTicketEvents, {awsS3Service: this.awsS3Service});{noformat}

And modify snapshot to parse comments and attachments so that comment_id and attachment_id are mandatory fields in snapshots' {{UserTicket}} interface.

+*AB analysis of the lost property process in place*+ 

* In the Uber case, it was determined that drivers should be classified as workers due to various factors, one of which was the significant control exerted by Uber. This control was examined through five key dimensions:

# Financial control
# Contractual control
# Acceptance of riders control
# Scope of services control
# Information control

* The court found that Uber's management practices, such as implementing performance evaluations and utiliising warning SMS messages with 'deactivation' as the ultimate consequence, influenced the way drivers performed their duties. This was one of the considerations that led the court to conclude that Uber drivers were not independent contractors but in fact workers.
* If Bolt is suspending drivers based on lost property issues (regardless of the specific lost items: keys, passports, ID etc), this could be seen as a form of 'scope of services control.' This is because, if drivers are independent contractors, they should have the freedom to conduct their business autonomously (the court will always look at the reality of what is happening in practice). Blocking drivers for lost property incidents (where the driver fails to respond to Bolt) appears to contradict this principle. 

In our view Bolt has no validating reason to penalise drivers for passengers lost property items, the reason being is Bolt has no way to determine if the item was left in the vehicle or not (the passenger may have lost the item an hour before entering the vehicle). In addition to that, there may be situations where passenger A leaves an item in the car (for example: ID/ mobile phone) and then after the trip is completed, passenger B enters the car and it is this passenger B who takes the item (as opposed to it being the driver). Because of this we do not feel that drivers should be penalised for this, it does not seem valid for Bolt to put the blame on drivers without having any substantiating evidence to support the blocking. 

+*What do the Driver Terms and Conditions say*+ 

* The terms and conditions do not mention anything about temporarily or permanently blocking drivers for failing to respond to inquiries about lost property. Currently, the practice is to block drivers based on the nature of the lost property item, but this is not documented in the T&Cs.
* Essentially this is a breach of section 9.e as there is no reference to drivers being blocked for lost property items. 
* Taking our T&Cs into account we do not have the right to block drivers for lost property matters it also increases the reclassification risks.

* However, if such actions are mandated by the regulatory authorities (as opposed to Bolt's discretionary choice), Bolt may defend any reclassification argument here by asserting that these measures are regulatory requirements imposed by the regulators. If this is the case, we should ensure that this is incorporated into the T&Cs.

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). 



So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

Q: Is there any loophole, whether on a global level or a market level, that would enable us:

* Download menu photos of Restaurant A from another platform
* Edit them (i.e. changing background)
* Upload the edited photos on Restaurant A's menu on our platform?

A: Use of third party photos requires permission from the copyright holder (other platform or restaurant). Downloading, editing and uploading photos without permission is usually copyright infringement. Depending on a market, the risk level varies from removing the infringing photos to payment of license fees. License fees can reach up to five figures per photo.More importantly, knowing infringement would significantly damage Bolt’s reputation.Only legal loopholes are:

* if the photos are not original. However, originality threshold is very low and usually infringers do not succeed in proving lack of originality. Also, I assume the number of photos would be high and therefore we would not have resources to determine originality of each photo;
* if photos are created by AI. AI created images are not protected by copyright (based on current laws, which may change in the future). Again, the question arises as to how to review each photo and decide whether or not it was made by AI.

I investigated this ticket and I found some issues. 

Context: in the past, device_id was required to send user funnel analytics events. However, we now save these types events in Presto. Therefore, even when device_id is undefined, we still need to publish the event to the Presto database. For Mixpanel (Rudderstack), device_id is required, so for older applications, we can simply filter this out. Actually, it works in a way that we always send analytic events to the “event” service. In the event service, the distinct_id is not checked, and events without a device_id can be sent to Rudderstack. In this case, device_id is required, which results in an invalid request error.

Examples when we send device_id = undefined:
*Old app versions* - when we don’t get distinct_id from the app. This is ok - we would like to have this events in Presto
*/mobility/appState/get/v1* - this request is call each time when user open the app. It mean that it is called for authorized and non-authorized users. For this endpoint we would like to log only not logged users and when users id is client-xxxxxxx we set distinct_id = undefined. But in this example we still send events to Presto so we should filter it out in different way. Maybe we can add simple enabled flag???
*profile/verification/confirm/v3 & profile/verification/start/v2*  - here we do the same as with getAppState request - we set distinct_id to undefined, but in this case it looks like a bad request from the mobile device. If the user is just starting login flow distinct_id should be random

Previous 2022 advice:

*Tying practice*

_In accordance with GO 99/2000 on marketing products and services to consumers, there is also a ban imposed upon retailers on tying the sale of a product with the sale of a another different product, i.e. if a consumer wants to buy tobacco only he/she should not be conditioned to buy another product, as well._

_Of course, it may be argued that this is not technically tying, since the consumer can buy cigarettes only. However, since cigarettes are not included in the minimum order value, the incentive to buy another product, as well, is greater than in the case of other non-tobacco products._

_Not least, from a practical perspective, Bolt's interpretation may not present relevance if, despite the discouraging action, consumers do actually buy cigarettes only. In this case, it will quite clear that Bolt is selling cigarettes at the regulated price plus a fee which is not transportation cost only._

*Fiscal risk*

_The reference to potential challenges referred to the authorities interpretation challenging Bolt's, so as to arrive to the conclusion that the cigarettes were sold above the maximum retail price._

_If this would be their conclusion, then the sanction for selling cigarettes above the maximum retail price is expressly provided in Art. 449 para. 3 of the Fiscal Code, i.e. a fine ranging from 20.000 and 100.000 lei (EUR 4.000 to EUR 20.000). The fiscal authorities may also confiscate the products or the proceeds resulted from their sale._

Hey Álvaro, here is a breakdown for your question:

“Ingresos Brutos” is the ride price before any discounts given to the rider, and it’s also the final price including VAT.

“IVA de transporte” is 10% *over the amount of the ride without VAT and after discounts*, because the only taxable amount is the one that we effectively charged (and goes to the invoice). 

So for example: 

Ride price: 20EUR

Campaigns: 3EUR

Then total to be paid by customer = 17 EUR

This 17 already includes VAT, so you would need to do (17 / 1.10) = 15.45 and this would be the taxable amount. 

15.45 * 0.10 = 1.54

So yeah, if you compare with the actual ride price which is 20 EUR, it always seems like we are charging less VAT, but it’s because we don’t show the breakdown of how we got to that final price (and we haven’t had any request to show it).

Let me know if you have more questions.

Cheers,

Hi [~accountid:5e7d11448f31f90c2f0daec0] and [~accountid:5fbb68f578f0180076139818] ,

Use of third party photos requires permission from the copyright holder (other platform or restaurant or any other third party). Downloading, editing and uploading photos without permission is usually copyright infringement. Depending on a market, the risk level varies from removing the infringing photos to payment of license fees + damage to Bolt’s reputation. License fees can reach up to five figures per photo. 

In your suggested approach, there is a risk that the photos are the IP of our competitors, so if they realise that we are using their photos, they can ask us to stop and, possibly, claim damages.

It is also possible that the IP of the photos belongs to the partners (instead of our competitors) and then we could use the photos with the partners' consent. However, it would be difficult to verify whether they actually own the IP rights (we would basically have to rely on their confirmation, which would be risky, as most partners probably don't know).

There are many different use cases where different options are optimal.

I shared some info here as well: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4603544138/2023-10+-+AWS+S3+bucket+use+cases#Options-for-access|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4603544138/2023-10+-+AWS+S3+bucket+use+cases#Options-for-access|smart-link] 

E.g. with Audio Trip Recording, we’re uploading big files which are split into smaller ones. To make it simpler, faster, and more cost-efficient we send files from the Driver App or Rider App directly to S3 bypassing our backend.

E.g. with [Driver Data Export Tool we’ll support multiple plugins|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4536861245/2023-08-22+Writing+Plugins+for+Driver+Data+Export+Tool] where it does not make sense for 1 service to upload everything - at least for bigger files.

Presigned URLs do not mean permanently shared access like a shared database - it means:

* for uploads, you’ll give the client access to write a new table isolated from everything else,
* for downloads, you’ll give the client read-only access to 1 row which is huge and you don’t wish to pass it through several layers.

Pass-through layers in our backend often also mean encoding/decoding with Base64 which is quite a mess.

Hi [~accountid:5f3a47cf91e67a003f9a9427] 

There is an existing risk within the business using Bolt Balance/promo codes as a form of refund. We have to pay any refunds (whether full or partial) back to the customer’s original payment method. For example, if they used a credit card to pay for a ride, any refund has to go back to the same credit card. We cannot, by default, pay refunds to a customer’s Bolt Balance Account/Promo Codes unless the customer has given their express consent for us to do this. Therefore if the customer is given a choice to have the refund on the original payment method, Bolt Balance or Promo Code and the customer chooses to have a promo code there is less risk. 

It is critical to our business that we comply with our legal obligations, to avoid claims against the business from individual customers and regulators (like Trading Standards and the Competition & Markets Authority), but also to show that we are meeting the standards expected by our licensing authorities when our operating licences come up for review and renewal. 

You mentioned that this is in situations where it is not possible to refund the customer in another way due to the customer leaving the country etc. Is this common and happening regularly or is this happening on a small scale? 

Depending on the volume of times this occurs and if you have a justified reason that we cannot refund the customer by another payment method and this happens in limited cases you can proceed to do this (knowing the risk). However, I would suggest keeping a record of the reason this method was used just in these cases so we have the information to pull in the event that we have to present it to any Trading Standards / Competition & Markets Authority, as this will help us justify the reason this was done. 

Please let me know if you need anything further. 

Thanks

Lets do that and we can then make changes for things that need based on the Pre-Hire setup.

We have 3 orthogonal concepts: client libraries, generated network api clients and compile-time sys2sys authorization. If you mix any pair of 2 out of those 3 concepts, they work fine. When you wanna have all 3 at the same time, you end up with a dependency problem: common code cannot depend on private apis, which are generated for each particular client. It’s a limitation of how compile-time sys2sys authorization is implemented.

Client libraries are not necessarily an anti-pattern, they can be very useful to solve certain problems. The issues comes from the implementation of the compile-time sys2sys authorization: it generally works, but it creates needless limitations / compatibility issues for the clients.

Atm, client libraries and compile-time sys2sys authorization are mutually exclusive, but they needn’t be because the concepts are not, only the implementation has a limitation, hence the ticket.

Thus, the platform cannot completely be left out, but the main responsibility is still on the seller and the courier. [Clause 2.8 of T&C for Partners|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/4zAJBa9sjUVOMHAEZ28ftE/7632198902976b0afbf39eac6a42e2b4/Bolt-Partner_General_Terms__EE__-ENG-EE-.docx.pdf] addresses this question:

These activities include verifying the minimum legal drinking age of the Client and ensuring compliance with the permitted hours for alcohol sales._+ _T_+_he Partner shall be fully responsible and indemnify Bolt against any allegations, claims, complaints or other matters from regulatory authorities_+ _or other third parties in relation to the sale of alcoholic beverages or any other regulated products in accordance with Section 12 of these General Terms”._

According to art. 11 of Law 15/99, it states in general terms that the communication of data between the data provider and the data transferee for the fulfilment of legitimate functions of both may only be carried out with the prior consent of the data subject. Article 11 sets out the exceptions to the need for the data subject's prior consent, which include communications to the Ombudsman, the Public Prosecutor's Office, Judges or Courts or the Court of Auditors, as well as autonomous institutions with similar functions to the first and last of the aforementioned institutions. Article 22 refers specifically to the files of the Security Forces and Corps. Geo services are offered as network apis, but a subset of those also available are offline libraries. _Example_: you can request an ETA to be calculated by Geo services and you get our best result, but there’s also the flight-distance ETA library that calculates an ETA between 2 points, but the accuracy is poor.

Geo clients (components of other teams that call Geo) implement a fallback mechanism many times over in all their components, so they would have some ETA instead of no ETA, in case there’s a failure on the Geo side. If we encapsulate that in a client library, then our clients wouldn’t need to worry about that, they would simply use our library. It would also make it much easier to add new alternatives to flight-distance ETA, as it would only require a configuration change in our client’s components. I looked further into the issue of Fuzzy name deduplication false positives
If we were to apply the idea of finding duplicates by “name + DoB + *document country*”, we would:

* Decrease the number of false positives from 27 to 3 in the last 3 months
* But increase significantly the number of false negatives (duplicate users not detected by the rule) by more than 400

In this case it’s better to stick with the current not-so-big number of false positives than to increase the number of false negatives.

About the ideas of improving the full name matching by doing an additional filtering on the response we got from ElasticSearch, I tried a few ideas, but couldn’t find a certain criteria that would lower the False Positives and not increase the False Negatives. Most of the approaches are a fine balance between the two. Also, I doubt we can beat ElasticSearch on fuzzy matching algorithm.

I did a rough estimation what it would take for us to implement face matching as an additional check. Probably it doesn’t make sense to implement it for this task now, but just to have an idea in case a similar discussion arises again later

There are two options (leaning towards the first one, but writing for reference):

* V1: Fallback for User duplicate check with AwsRekognition provider
** We can use the fallback mechanism to avoid some unnecessary tasks spawning and coupling between different providers
** Estimated effort: ~1.6 m/w
** Drawback: we can do it only for one pair of selfies. If we have multiple duplicate flow runs found, we need to choose only one.
* V2: spawn tasks for face match within Veritas provider
** Estimated effort: 4 m/d
** We can have as many face match tasks as needed
** Drawback: creating two types of tasks that do pretty much the same thing (we’ll reuse the code, but not sure how good it would be from analytics point of view)

*Rider relocation incentives*

Tallinn. Count of cases when car was idling between rides for 24-72h (more than 72 - probably service): 

* 6059 in the last 3 months. 
* Avg idle time was 38h.
* On avg in 38h (1.5 days) car makes 8 rides. 
* That means in the last 3 months 8 * 6059 = 48K rides were lost, out of 484K rides (10% of rides were lost due to cars being in bad locations).

If we give users discount of 30% and in 30% of cases we’ll be able to reduce the idle time by 50%, then we’ll get 30%*50%*10% = 1.5% more rides. But, as discount is 30%, then *GMV impact is 1.5%*(100%-30%)=1.05%*

You can play with assumptions (30%,30%,50%) to get better results, but i think that’s reasonable)

Hi [~accountid:6409fe939ce2cd2c241185cb] reverting to the matter after my vacation. 

By way of the clarification:

* by “courier” in [the Courier T&C|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/3l0HPdLMbiWTt0eyyzFGr6/V4%20of%20Bolt-Courier%20T%26C%20(SK)%20-SK-.pdf] we understand: “_the entity any natural person who owns an entrepreneur account, sole entrepreneur or legal entity and where relevant, its employees and/or contractors, who have been registered in the Bolt Food Platform as a provider of the delivery service to the Client with respect to Goods ordered through the Bolt Food Platform.” -_ 
* hence - in case of the fleet couriers - no individual courier, but the fleet. Therefore, whenever we refer to the “courier” in the Courier T&C, we mean the fleet. This means that the termination right in clause 9.2 should also refer to the fleet, not an individual courier. 

In general, in case of the fleet couriers, formally we have a legal cooperation with the fleet and fleet provides the delivery services via its employees / contractors - i.e. individual couriers. Therefore, we cannot “end the cooperation” with the fleet courier directly, since the courier is not a party to the cooperation with Bolt.

However, for the safety reasons, we can block (permanently or temporarily) the courier in case of any safety reasons which justify the immediate reaction. Some time ago we commented [the blocking guidelines|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/16gYO1uUeL1hrL5T55bNwcnu0V4_13AglHbGj0jvntnc/edit?usp=sharing] with [~accountid:62e3c9015f7842fb12948c84]- not sure what is the status of the document?

Please let me know if you have any further question - I understand that this matter might be not clear, but perhaps we can find solutions which address the business concerns.
